On August 15, 2025 at approximately 6:30pm our 2024 BMW i7 eDrive50 with the Active Park Distance Control package accelerated in reverse when parking assistance was initiated to back out of a parking space at a small business facility, causing the vehicle to strike a tree. The cronology of the incident is as follows: 1. While the driver had his foot on the brake, he touched the assisted parking icon on the dashboard display to enable the automatic backup system. 2. The driver then lifted his foot from the brake and the vehicle accelerated in reverse despite the driver NOT having his foot on the gas pedal. 3. The backup camera did not engage or show the backup view when the car was moving quickly in reverse. 4. The driver slammed on the brake just as the vehicle struck a tree with the rear right bumper and panel. In summary, the automated parking space back up feature malfunctioned by accelerating in reverse while the driver's foot was not on the gas pedal. Simultaneously, the back up camera did not engage to show the rear view while the vehicle was moving in reverse. This malfunction created a safety risk that could have put other vehicles, people or property at risk of damage or injury, beyond the estimated $8,000-$10,000 damage sustained by this BMW i7. A certified BMW collision repair facility has inspected this vehicle and are awaiting inspection from BMW customer support. The collision repair facility was not able to find a video of the incident in the vehicle camera history files or in any alerts. The driver has not attempted to reproduce the malfunction. The vehicle is awaiting inspection from BMW customer support.  There were no warning lamps or messages displayed during or after the accident.  BMW customer support has been contacted.

signals.title: Interior is very comfortable and luxurious
signals.summary: Customers consistently say the cabin is extremely comfortable and feels very luxurious. Comfort is often called a standout attribute, with drivers praising the relaxed ride, rear-seat comfort, and suitability for long trips.

signals.title: Most comfortable seats I have ever experienced
signals.summary: Customers say the seats are extremely comfortable and often the most comfortable they have ever sat in. They note improvements over prior models and competitors, and praise the rear seats for long trips and a very luxurious feel.

signals.summary: Customers consistently say the cabin feels very roomy and comfortable. They praise the generous legroom and space for passengers, noting the back seat impresses guests and tall riders feel well accommodated.

signals.summary: Customers report the air conditioning is weak and slow to cool the cabin, even when max settings are used. They say vents do not deliver enough airflow, rear passengers get less cooling, and some areas of the cabin receive little or no air. signals.title: Really enjoy the ambient lighting
signals.summary: Customers say the ambient lighting makes the cabin feel special and enhances the night experience. They praise the roof LEDs, the jewelry-style crystal welcome lights, and the color-changing options that are fun to switch.

signals.title: I really love the automatic doors
signals.summary: Customers say the automatic doors are convenient and they really enjoy using them. They like that doors open and close with a button or by pressing the brake, appreciate the soft close, and find it helpful when hands are full or when helping children.

signals.title: Infotainment system is too complicated
signals.summary: Customers say the operating system is hard to learn and not intuitive. They report buried menus, too many steps and icons, and that reliance on the touchscreen makes controls distracting or harder to use, with several customers wanting physical buttons, easier shortcuts, or better app organization. signals.title: Ride is incredibly smooth and comfortable
signals.summary: Customers say the suspension and cushioning make the ride extremely smooth and comfortable. They describe a floating, luxurious feel, excellent bump absorption, and strong comfort on long trips.

signals.title: Enjoy the various driving modes
signals.summary: Customers love switching among driving modes and enjoy experimenting with My Modes. They say the modes noticeably change the car’s feel and positioning, delivering everything from sporty, fun performance to smooth, comfortable driving.

signals.title: All the technology is phenomenal
signals.summary: Customers praise the car's technology as advanced, easy to use, and a standout part of the ownership experience. They appreciate the wide range of features, frequent updates, and consistent, reliable operation.

signals.title: Seats are uncomfortable and hard to adjust

signals.summary: For the 2025–2026 US Mercedes‑Benz EQS, Mercedes fits the MBUX Hyperscreen: three active displays (12.3" driver + 17.7" center + 12.3" passenger) under a single curved glass measuring over 55–56 inches across the dash. Mercedes has moved many formerly physical controls into the EQS central touchscreen and steering touch surfaces, leaving relatively few hard buttons on the dash or center stack. Multiple professional reviews and owner reports say MBUX and the Hyperscreen offer extensive functionality but have a steep learning curve and can hide commonly used functions several menu levels deep, which some users describe as 'tricky' or 'complex' to use.

signals.title: Audi A8: eSIM setup is a nightmare and unreliable
signals.summary: Audi's current MMI 'touch response' infotainment architecture (used on the A8) pairs a 12.3‑inch Audi Virtual Cockpit Plus instrument display with two center touchscreen panels — a 10.1‑inch upper screen for navigation/media and an 8.6‑inch lower screen for climate/comfort — and the platform (MIB 3) uses an Online Connectivity Unit (OCU) that includes an integrated eSIM and a built‑in Wi‑Fi hotspot option. Edmunds’ 2024/2025 coverage and aggregated owner feedback list a steep infotainment learning curve and electrical/software complaints among common owner criticisms for the A8 (noting a 'steep infotainment learning curve' and occasional electrical gremlins in owner reports). BMW’s G70 7 Series (the 2023‑onward 7 Series family) uses BMW’s Curved Display — a large, driver‑facing panel pairing a 12.3‑inch digital instrument cluster with a 14.9‑inch infotainment touchscreen — and runs BMW’s iDrive 8 (touchscreen + voice + controller/rotary input) interface with extensive rear‑seat touchscreen and entertainment options available.

signals.title: Lucid Air: Screen cluttered and hard to use while driving
signals.summary: The Lucid Air uses a 34‑inch curved “Glass Cockpit” display assembly that integrates the driver instrument cluster and the main infotainment area across the dash. Multiple professional reviews describe Lucid’s native infotainment as “menu‑heavy” with many functions buried in layers, and note that many users default to Apple CarPlay/Android Auto rather than the native UI because of that complexity. Consumer Reports’ Lucid Air road test criticizes having to adjust items such as the steering wheel and side mirrors through the infotainment touchscreen, calling that a prolonged driver distraction and a nuisance.

signals.title: Genesis G90: Seats are uncomfortable and hard to adjust
signals.summary: Major U.S. expert reviews describe the Genesis G90’s front and outboard rear seats as feature‑rich and generally ‘plush’—standard Nappa leather with heated, ventilated and massage functions and multi‑way powered adjustments—making it a comfort‑focused cabin in road tests of the 2024–2026 G90.  Genesis’ official specifications list trunk (cargo) volume for the G90 as about 12.0 cu ft for the base 3.5T and 10.6 cu ft for the E‑Supercharged/mild‑hybrid variant (U.S. spec sheet).

signals.title: Mercedes-Benz S-Class: Doesn't connect or connects inconsistently
signals.summary: Mercedes-Benz markets the 2026 S‑Class with a new MB.OS architecture and a standard MBUX Superscreen that combines a 14.4‑inch central display and a 12.3‑inch front passenger display, plus a 12.3‑inch driver display option (including an optional 3D instrument cluster). BMW offers Remote Software Upgrade (over‑the‑air software updates) specifically to deliver infotainment and operating‑system fixes and feature improvements (BMW lists multiple RSU release notes and encourages installing RSUs to address functional issues). Independent industry research (JD Power U.S. Multimedia Quality and Satisfaction Study, Sept 12, 2024) documents that multimedia/infotainment problems increased in prior years and that further optimization of Apple CarPlay and Android Auto remains a top industry priority — i.e., inconsistent phone‑projection connectivity is a recognized, cross‑OEM issue.

signals.title: Audi A8: Include a spare and better tire options
signals.summary: Car and Driver’s 2025 review describes the Audi A8’s exterior as “reserved and stately,” noting the A8 ‘‘flies too far under the radar’’ compared with rivals such as the BMW 7‑series (i.e., the A8’s styling is more understated in the US 2025 market). Audi’s own 2021 press release for the enhanced A8 describes the A8 exterior as ‘‘representative, confident, and athletic’’ with a sharpened front and rear design, new headlight/taillight signatures and wheel choices (Audi’s presentation positions the A8 as a more restrained, refined flagship rather than an overtly extroverted statement).

signals.title: Trend 2028-2031: range_charging
signals.summary: Network connector access: major U.S. charging networks and equipment vendors announced plans in 2023–2025 to add Tesla’s NACS connector to their portfolios (Electrify America, ChargePoint, EVgo and others), and most large OEMs announced NACS adoption for North America — which improves charging access for premium cars that switch to NACS or for networks that install NACS ports between 2025 and the late 2020s. (announcement example: Electrify America plan to add NACS plugs).

signals.title: Trend 2028-2031: infotainment_digital
signals.summary: Automakers have publicly reversed purely ‘buttonless’ designs (for example Mercedes-Benz has said it will restore essential tactile buttons), signalling that premium brands selling in the US will reintroduce tactile controls alongside large displays during the 2028–2031 timeframe.

signals.title: Trend 2028-2031: interior
signals.summary: Automotive strategy/consulting analyses (McKinsey) and industry‑design coverage report that electrification plus higher levels of automation enable ‘lounge‑like’ and multi‑use interiors (flexible seating arrangements, flat floors, modular furniture) — concepts that premium‑segment OEMs are prototyping and that analysts expect to influence production designs in the late‑2020s/early‑2030s (this is an industry inference supported by cited analyses and concept examples).

signals.title: Trend 2028-2031: driver_assistance
signals.summary: McKinsey’s industry analysis projects strong growth of advanced ADAS and estimates that by 2030 roughly 12% of vehicles could be equipped with Level‑3/4 capabilities (while Level‑2+ will dominate broader market adoption), supporting the expectation that Level‑3/hands‑off features will be present but limited in market share by 2030.
